title.zh: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉
title.en: Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十七 蹇義 夏原吉 Volume 149 Biographies 37: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji

sentences.zh: 蹇義夏原吉

translations.literal: Jian Yi [and] Xia Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the subsection.

sentences.zh: （俞士吉李文郁鄒師顏）〉

translations.literal: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)〉
translations.idiomatic: (See also the biographies of Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, and Zou Shiyan.)〉

sentences.zh: 燕師入，迎附，遷左侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Yan army entered, [he] welcomed [them] and submitted; he was transferred to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army entered the capital, he welcomed the new regime and was appointed Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 數月，進尚書。

translations.literal: After several months, he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 時方務反建文之政，所更易者悉罷之。

translations.literal: At that time they were bent on reversing the Jianwen emperor's policies; whatever had been changed was all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then intent on reversing the policies of the Jianwen reign, and every measure that had been altered was abolished wholesale.

sentences.zh: 義從容言曰：「損益貴適時宜。

translations.literal: Yi said calmly: "Increase and decrease value timeliness and appropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said evenly, "What to add or cut should be judged by what suits the times.

sentences.zh: 前改者固不當，今必欲盡復者，亦未悉當也。

translations.literal: The former changes were indeed improper; now if one must fully restore everything, that too is not entirely appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier reforms were indeed wrong, but to insist now on restoring everything is not necessarily right either.

sentences.zh: 」因舉數事陳說本末。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he cited several matters and set forth their background from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited several cases and explained how each had come about.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised [it] as good and followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he was also made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2 he was additionally appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝有所傳諭太子，輒遣義，能委曲導意。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor had something to convey to the heir, he always sent Yi, who could tactfully guide the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor wished to instruct the heir, he sent Jian, who could convey the intent with tact and finesse.

sentences.zh: 帝與太子俱愛重之。

translations.literal: Both the emperor and the heir held him in affection and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Both emperor and heir held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝巡北京，命輔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor toured Beijing and ordered [him] to assist the heir in governing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the emperor went to Beijing, he was ordered to assist the heir in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 義熟典故，達治體，軍國事皆倚辦。

translations.literal: Yi was versed in precedents and understood the structure of governance; military and state affairs all relied on him to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was steeped in precedent and understood how government worked; military and civil affairs alike were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 時舊臣見親用者，戶部尚書夏原吉與義齊名，中外稱曰「蹇、夏」。

translations.literal: Among old ministers then in close use, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji was of equal fame with Yi; within and without they were called "Jian and Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Among the veteran ministers then in favor, Minister of Revenue Xia Yuanji stood equal with Jian in renown; court and country called them "Jian and Xia."

sentences.zh: 滿三考，帝親宴二人便殿，褒揚甚至。

translations.literal: When three terms of assessment were complete, the emperor personally feasted the two men in the side hall and praised them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When their three-year assessments were complete, the emperor personally entertained them in the side hall and praised them at length.

sentences.zh: 數奉命兼理他部事，職務填委，處之裕如。

translations.literal: Several times he received orders to handle other ministries' affairs concurrently; duties piled up, yet he handled them with ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to take charge of other ministries as well; though duties piled upon him, he managed them with ease.

sentences.zh: 十七年以父喪歸，帝及太子皆遣官賜祭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned on his father's mourning; the emperor and the heir both sent officials with sacrificial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he went home for his father's mourning; both emperor and heir sent officials with offerings.

sentences.zh: 詔起復。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him from mourning to office.

sentences.zh: 十九年，三殿災，敕廷臣二十六人巡行天下。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the three main halls burned; twenty-six court ministers were ordered to tour the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when fire destroyed the three main halls, twenty-six court ministers were ordered to tour the empire.

sentences.zh: 義及給事中馬俊分巡應天諸府，問軍民疾苦，黜文武長吏擾民者數人，條興革數十事奏行之。

translations.literal: Yi and supervising secretary Ma Jun toured the prefectures of Yingtian, inquired into the sufferings of soldiers and civilians, dismissed several civil and military chief officials who harassed the people, and listed dozens of matters to institute or abolish, memorializing them for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and supervising secretary Ma Jun toured the prefectures around Yingtian, inquired into the hardships of soldiers and civilians, dismissed several civil and military chiefs who harassed the people, and submitted dozens of proposals for reform, which were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 還治部事。

translations.literal: He returned to administer his ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to his ministry duties.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝北征還，以太子曲宥呂震婿主事張鶴朝參失儀，罪義不匡正，逮義系錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: The next year, when the emperor returned from the northern campaign, because the heir had bent the rules to spare Lü Zhen's son-in-law, director Zhang He, for impropriety at court audience, Yi was blamed for not correcting [it] and was arrested and held in the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the emperor returned from the northern campaign, the heir had bent the rules to spare Lü Zhen's son-in-law Zhang He for impropriety at audience. Jian was blamed for failing to correct this and was imprisoned in the Brocade Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 又明年春得釋。

translations.literal: The spring of the year after next he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released the following spring.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，義、原吉皆以元老為中外所信。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Yi and Yuanji were both trusted within and without as senior elders.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, both Jian and Yuanji were trusted throughout the realm as elder statesmen.

sentences.zh: 帝又念義監國時舊勞，尤厚倚之。

translations.literal: The emperor also recalled Yi's old labors during the regency and relied on him all the more heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also remembered Jian's service during the regency and relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 首進義少保，賜冠服、象笏、玉帶，兼食二祿。

translations.literal: He first promoted Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowing court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, with emoluments from two offices.
translations.idiomatic: He first promoted Jian to Junior Guardian, granting court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, with emoluments from two offices.

sentences.zh: 歷進少師，賜銀章一，文曰「繩愆糾繆」。

translations.literal: He was advanced in turn to Junior Preceptor and given one silver seal inscribed "Correct faults and rectify errors."
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Junior Preceptor and given a silver seal inscribed "Correct faults and rectify errors."

sentences.zh: 已，復賜璽書曰：「曩朕監國，卿以先朝舊臣，日侍左右。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again bestowed a sealed letter saying: "Formerly when I governed the realm, you as an old minister of the previous reign attended me daily at my side.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted another sealed letter: "When I governed the realm as heir, you, an old minister of the previous reign, attended me day after day.

sentences.zh: 兩京肇建，政務方殷，卿勞心焦思，不恤身家，二十余年，夷險一節。

translations.literal: As the two capitals were first built and state affairs were pressing, you labored in mind and burned in thought, heedless of self and family; for more than twenty years, through ease and peril alike, one constant integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As the two capitals were built and affairs pressed upon us, you toiled without regard for yourself or your family. For more than twenty years, through calm and crisis alike, your constancy never wavered.

sentences.zh: 朕承大統，贊襄治理，不懈益恭。

translations.literal: I have received the great succession and you assist in governance, unceasing and ever more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne you have aided my rule, tireless and ever more devoted.

sentences.zh: 朕篤念不忘，茲以已意，創制『蹇忠貞印』賜卿。

translations.literal: I cherish this deeply and do not forget; now by my own intent I have newly made the "Seal of Jian's Loyalty and Integrity" to bestow on you.
translations.idiomatic: I hold this in deep remembrance. By my own wish I have had made the "Seal of Jian's Loyalty and Integrity" and grant it to you.

sentences.zh: 俾藏於家，傳之後世，知朕君臣共濟艱難，相與有成也。

translations.literal: Let it be kept in your house and passed to later generations, so they may know that ruler and minister together braved hardship and achieved success together.
translations.idiomatic: Keep it in your house and pass it to posterity, so they may know how we ruler and minister shared hardship and achieved success together."

sentences.zh: 」時惟楊士奇亦得賜「貞一」印及敕。

translations.literal: " At that time only Yang Shiqi also received the "Integrity and Unity" seal and an edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Yang Shiqi likewise received the "Integrity and Unity" seal and an edict.

sentences.zh: 尋命與英國公輔及原吉同監修《太宗實錄》。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying Fu and Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong》.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying and Xia Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong》.

sentences.zh: 義視原吉尤重厚，然過於周慎。

translations.literal: Yi regarded Yuanji as especially weighty and substantial, yet he was overly thorough and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Jian esteemed Yuanji as especially solid and dependable, yet he himself was overly cautious in every detail.

sentences.zh: 士奇嘗於帝前謂義曰：「何過慮？

translations.literal: Shiqi once said to Yi before the emperor: "Why such excessive worry?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi once said to Jian before the emperor, "Why worry so much?

sentences.zh: 」義曰：「恐鹵莽為後憂耳。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "I fear rashness may become a worry for later."
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "I fear that rashness today may bring trouble tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 」帝兩是之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both views.

sentences.zh: 楊榮嘗毀義。

translations.literal: Yang Rong once slandered Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong once spoke ill of Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝不直榮。

translations.literal: The emperor did not side with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept Rong's account.

sentences.zh: 義頓首言：「榮無他。

translations.literal: Yi kowtowed and said: "Rong has no other [intent].
translations.idiomatic: Jian kowtowed and said, "Rong means no harm.

sentences.zh: 即左右有讒榮者，願陛下慎察。

translations.literal: If those at your side should slander Rong, I beg Your Majesty to examine carefully.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone at your side speaks against him, I beg Your Majesty to look closely before you judge."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「吾固弗信也。

translations.literal: " The emperor smiled and said: "I never believed it in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "I never believed it in the first place."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗即位，委寄益重。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, his trust and charge grew still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, his reliance on Jian grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 時方修獻陵，帝欲遵遺詔從儉約，以問義、原吉。

translations.literal: At that time they were building the Xian Mausoleum; the emperor wished to follow the testamentary edict in frugal simplicity and asked Yi and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: While the Xian Mausoleum was under construction, the emperor wished to follow the late emperor's testament and keep it frugal, and consulted Jian and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 二人力贊曰：「聖見高遠，出於至孝，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: The two strongly praised, saying: "Your sage vision is lofty and far-reaching, arising from utmost filial piety; it is a benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both strongly endorsed the plan: "Your vision is far-sighted and born of deepest filial piety; it will benefit generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」帝親為規畫，三月而陵成，宏麗不及長陵，其後諸帝因以為制。

translations.literal: " The emperor personally planned it; in three months the mausoleum was complete, its grandeur not reaching the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took it as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally oversaw the design. The tomb was finished in three months—splendid, but less grand than the Chang Mausoleum—and later emperors took this as the model."

sentences.zh: 迨世宗營永陵，始益崇侈雲。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Shizong built the Yong Mausoleum did extravagance grow still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Shizong built the Yong Mausoleum did tombs grow markedly more lavish.

sentences.zh: 帝征樂安，義、原吉及諸學士皆從，預軍中機務，賜鞍馬甲胄弓劍。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Le'an, Yi, Yuanji, and the various academicians all followed, taking part in military counsels, and were bestowed saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Le'an, Jian, Yuanji, and the academicians accompanied him, took part in military planning, and were granted saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.

sentences.zh: 及還，賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: When they returned, rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, the rewards were exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 三年從巡邊還。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned from accompanying the border tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned from accompanying the border inspection.

sentences.zh: 帝以義、原吉、士奇、榮四人者皆已老，賜璽書曰：「卿等皆祖宗遺老，畀輔朕躬。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yi, Yuanji, Shiqi, and Rong were all already old, bestowed a sealed letter saying: "You are all surviving elders left by our forefathers, entrusted to assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Jian, Yuanji, Shiqi, and Rong were all advanced in years, the emperor granted a sealed letter: "You are elders left by our forefathers to assist me.

sentences.zh: 今黃髮危齒，不宜復典冗劇，傷朝廷優老待賢之禮。

translations.literal: Now with yellow hair and tottering teeth, it is not fitting to again preside over tedious and heavy duties, harming the court's ritual of honoring the aged and treating the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Your hair is white and your steps unsteady; it is no longer fitting that you bear heavy routine duties, to the detriment of the court's duty to honor age and worth.

sentences.zh: 可輟所務，朝夕在朕左右討論至理，共寧邦家。

translations.literal: You may leave off your tasks and morning and evening be at my side discussing supreme principle, together bringing peace to state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Lay aside your offices and remain at my side morning and evening to discuss great affairs, so that together we may secure the realm."

sentences.zh: 官祿悉如舊。

translations.literal: Official salaries were all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Your salaries and rank would remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」明年，郭琎代為尚書。

translations.literal: " The next year Guo Jin replaced [him] as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Guo Jin replaced him as minister.

sentences.zh: 尋以胡濙言，命義等四人議天下官吏軍民建言章奏。

translations.literal: Soon, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the four—Yi and the others—were ordered to deliberate on memorials and submissions from officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Hu Ying's advice, Jian and the other three were ordered to review memorials from officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 復賜義銀章，文曰「忠厚寬宏」。

translations.literal: Yi was again given a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was again granted a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."

sentences.zh: 七年詔有司為義營新第於文明門內。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the relevant offices to build Yi a new residence inside the Wenhua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict ordered officials to build Jian a new residence inside the Wenhua Gate.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，齋宿得疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, [Yi] fell ill while observing purification rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Jian fell ill while observing ritual purification.

sentences.zh: 遣醫往視，問所欲言。

translations.literal: Physicians were sent to see him and asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians were sent to attend him and asked whether he had anything to say.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下初嗣大寶，望敬守祖宗成憲，始終不渝耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has newly succeeded to the great treasure; I hope you will respectfully keep the established statutes of the ancestors, from beginning to end without change."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has newly taken the throne. I beg you to honor and keep the institutions of our ancestors, unchanged to the end."

sentences.zh: 」遂卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongding (Loyal and Settled).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Settled.

sentences.zh: 義為人質直孝友，善處僚友間，未嘗一語傷物。

translations.literal: Yi as a man was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; he was skilled in dealings among colleagues and never once spoke a word that harmed others.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; he handled relations among colleagues well and never spoke a word that wounded another.

sentences.zh: 士奇常言：「張詠之不飾玩好，傅堯俞之遇人以誠，範景仁之不設城府，義兼有之。

translations.literal: Shiqi often said: "Zhang Yong's not adorning himself with curios, Fu Yaoyu's treating people with sincerity, Fan Jingren's not setting up inner and outer walls—Yi combined them all."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's disdain for ornament, Fu Yaoyu's sincerity toward others, Fan Jingren's open heart—Jian possessed all three."

sentences.zh: 」子英，有詩名，以蔭為尚寶司丞，歷官太常少卿。

translations.literal: " His son Ying had a name in poetry; by hereditary privilege he became vice commissioner of the Imperial Seals Office and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying was known as a poet; by hereditary privilege he became vice commissioner of the Imperial Seals Office and eventually Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉，字維喆，其先德興人。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji, style name Weizhe, his ancestors were men of Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji, courtesy name Weizhe, came of a family from Dexing.

sentences.zh: 父時敏，官湘陰教諭，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Shimin served as instructor in Xiangyin and thereupon made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shimin was an instructor in Xiangyin, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 原吉早孤，力學養母。

translations.literal: Yuanji was orphaned early, studied hard, and supported his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji lost his father early, studied diligently, and supported his mother.

sentences.zh: 以鄉薦入太學，選入禁中書制誥。

translations.literal: By provincial recommendation he entered the Imperial Academy and was selected to draft edicts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended from his district, he entered the Imperial Academy and was chosen to draft edicts in the palace.

sentences.zh: 諸生或喧笑，原吉危坐儼然。

translations.literal: When fellow students sometimes laughed and clamored, Yuanji sat upright in formal posture.
translations.idiomatic: While other students laughed and talked, Yuanji sat upright and composed.

sentences.zh: 太祖诇而異之。

translations.literal: Taizu observed this and regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu noticed and took him for remarkable.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 曹務叢脞，處之悉有條理，尚書郁新甚重之。

translations.literal: Department business was tangled and complex; he handled it all with order, and Minister Yu Xin greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Though ministry business was tangled and heavy, he handled everything in good order, and Minister Yu Xin held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 有劉郎中者，忌其能。

translations.literal: There was a Director Liu who envied his ability.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Director Liu envied his talent.

sentences.zh: 會新劾諸司怠事者。

translations.literal: It happened that Xin impeached those in various offices who neglected their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xin impeached officials in various offices for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 帝欲宥之，新持不可。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to pardon them; Xin insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to pardon them, but Xin refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問：「誰教若？

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and asked: "Who taught you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and demanded, "Who put you up to this?

sentences.zh: 」新頓首曰：「堂後書算生。

translations.literal: " Xin kowtowed and said: "The clerks and calculators behind the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xin kowtowed and answered, "The clerks behind the hall."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃下書算生於獄。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon put the clerks and calculators in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had those clerks imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 劉郎中遂言：「教尚書者，原吉也。

translations.literal: Director Liu then said: "The one who instructed the Minister was Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu then said, "It was Yuanji who advised the minister."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「原吉能佐尚書理部事，汝欲陷之耶！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Yuanji can assist the Minister in managing the ministry's affairs—do you wish to entrap him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yuanji helps the minister run this ministry—do you mean to ruin him?"

sentences.zh: 」劉郎中與書算生皆棄市。

translations.literal: " Director Liu and the clerks and calculators were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Director Liu and the clerks were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 建文初，擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianwen reign he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年充采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he served as investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 巡福建，所過郡邑，核吏治，咨民隱。

translations.literal: Touring Fujian, in every prefecture and district he passed he examined officials' governance and inquired into the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Fujian, he examined local governance and heard the people's grievances in every prefecture and county he visited.

sentences.zh: 人皆悅服。

translations.literal: All were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All were won over.

sentences.zh: 久之，移駐蘄州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to be stationed at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，或執原吉以獻。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, some seized Yuanji to present [him as a captive].
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu took the throne, some seized Yuanji to present him as a captive.

sentences.zh: 帝釋之，轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor released him and transferred him to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released him and appointed him Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 或言原吉建文時用事，不可信。

translations.literal: Some said that during Jianwen Yuanji had held power and could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that Yuanji had held power under Jianwen and could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，與蹇義同進尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen and promoted him to Minister together with Jian Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed and promoted him to minister together with Jian Yi.

sentences.zh: 偕義等詳定賦役諸制。

translations.literal: Together with Yi and others he worked out in detail the regulations on taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Jian and others he worked out the regulations on taxes and corvée labor in detail.

sentences.zh: 建白三十余事，皆簡便易遵守。

translations.literal: He proposed more than thirty measures, all simple, convenient, and easy to observe.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed more than thirty measures, all simple and easy to enforce.

sentences.zh: 曰：「行之而難繼者，且重困民，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: He said: "Those that in practice would be hard to continue would only further burden the people—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Measures that would be hard to sustain in practice would only burden the people further, and I cannot bear that."

sentences.zh: 」浙西大水，有司治不效。

translations.literal: " Western Zhejiang suffered great flood; the authorities' remedies were ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang suffered severe flooding, and local officials could not control it.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，命原吉治之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle Yuanji was ordered to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he was ordered to take charge of the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍郎李文郁為之副，復使僉都御史俞士吉賫水利書賜之。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered [that] Vice Minister Li Wenyu serve as his deputy; again he sent Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji bearing a treatise on water control to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Minister Li Wenyu was appointed his deputy, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Shiji was again dispatched to present him with an imperial treatise on waterworks.

sentences.zh: 原吉請循禹三江入海故跡，浚吳淞下流，上接太湖，而度地為閘，以時蓄泄。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested following the old traces by which Yu's three rivers entered the sea, dredging the lower reaches of Wusong, linking upward to Tai Lake, and measuring the ground to set sluice gates for timely impounding and release.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji proposed restoring the old course by which Yu the Great's three rivers had reached the sea: dredging the lower Wusong, connecting it upstream to Tai Lake, and building sluice gates at measured points to store and release water as seasons required.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 役十余萬人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand men were conscripted for labor.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand men were put to work.

sentences.zh: 原吉布衣徒步，日夜經畫。

translations.literal: Yuanji went in plain cloth and on foot, planning day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji wore plain clothes, walked on foot, and directed the work day and night.

sentences.zh: 盛暑不張蓋，曰：「民勞，吾何忍獨適。

translations.literal: In great heat he did not open a parasol, saying: "The people toil—how could I bear to enjoy comfort alone?
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer he would not raise a sunshade, saying, "The people are laboring—how can I alone seek ease?"

sentences.zh: 」事竣，還京師，言水雖由故道入海，而支流未盡疏泄，非經久計。

translations.literal: " When the work was finished he returned to the capital and said that although the water now entered the sea by the old channel, tributary streams had not all been cleared and drained—a plan not fit to last.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he returned to the capital and reported that although the main channel again reached the sea, tributaries were still not fully cleared and drained, and this was no lasting remedy.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，原吉復行，浚白茆塘、劉家河、大黃浦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Yuanji set out again to dredge Baimao Pond, Liujia River, and the Great Huangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Yuanji went out again to dredge Baimao Pond, the Liujia River, and the Great Huangpu.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿袁復為之副。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Fu was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 已，復命陜西參政宋性佐之。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered [that] Shaanxi Administrative Commissioner Song Xing assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shaanxi Administrative Commissioner Song Xing was also ordered to assist him.

sentences.zh: 九月工畢，水泄，蘇、松農田大利。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the work was finished, water drained off, and farmlands in Suzhou and Songjiang greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month the work was complete, the waters had drained, and the fields of Suzhou and Songjiang profited greatly.

sentences.zh: 三年還。

translations.literal: After three years he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he returned.

sentences.zh: 其夏，浙西大饑。

translations.literal: That summer western Zhejiang suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That summer western Zhejiang was stricken with severe famine.

sentences.zh: 命原吉率俞士吉、袁復及左通政趙居任往振，發粟三十萬石，給牛種。

translations.literal: Yuanji was ordered to lead Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Commissioner Zhao Juren to provide relief, distributing three hundred thousand shi of grain and supplying oxen and seed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was ordered to lead Yu Shiji, Yuan Fu, and Left Commissioner Zhao Juren in famine relief, distributing three hundred thousand shi of grain and providing oxen and seed.

sentences.zh: 有請召民佃水退淤田益賦者，原吉馳疏止之。

translations.literal: When someone proposed calling on the people to farm silted fields left by receding floodwater and increase the tax levy, Yuanji sent an urgent memorial to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed summoning the people to cultivate newly exposed silt fields and raise the tax assessment, Yuanji sent an urgent memorial to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝還自浙西，稱原吉曰：「古之遺愛也。

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao returned from western Zhejiang and praised Yuanji, saying: "A kindness from antiquity that survives in memory.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from western Zhejiang, Yao Guangxiao praised Yuanji, saying, "This is the enduring benevolence of the ancients."

sentences.zh: 」亡何，郁新卒，召還，理部事。

translations.literal: " Before long Yu Xin died; [Yuanji] was recalled to manage the affairs of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu Xin died, and Yuanji was recalled to manage the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 首請裁冗食，平賦役；

translations.literal: He first requested cutting redundant sinecures and leveling taxes and corvée;
translations.idiomatic: His first proposals were to cut redundant posts and equalize taxes and corvée labor;

sentences.zh: 嚴鹽法、錢鈔之禁；

translations.literal: tightening prohibitions on the salt laws and paper currency;
translations.idiomatic: to enforce the salt laws and restrictions on coin and paper money;

sentences.zh: 清倉場，廣屯種，以給邊蘇民，且便商賈。

translations.literal: clearing granary depots, expanding garrison farming, to supply the frontier and relieve the people, and also to facilitate merchants.
translations.idiomatic: to clear the granary depots and expand garrison farming, thereby supplying the frontier, easing the people's burden, and aiding merchants.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 凡中外戶口、府庫、田賦贏縮之數，各以小簡書置懷中，時檢閱之。

translations.literal: All figures on households within and without, treasuries and storehouses, and surplus or deficit in land tax he wrote each on small slips and kept them in his breast, reviewing them from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the figures for households across the empire, treasuries, storehouses, and gains and losses in land tax on small slips, kept them in his robe, and reviewed them constantly.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝問：「天下錢、谷幾何？

translations.literal: One day the emperor asked: "How much money and grain are there under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked, "How much money and grain does the realm hold?"

sentences.zh: 」對甚悉，以是益重之。

translations.literal: " He answered in great detail, and for this the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji answered in full detail, and the emperor came to rely on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 當是時，兵革初定，論「靖難」功臣封賞，分封諸藩，增設武衛百司。

translations.literal: At that time, when warfare had just settled, they deliberated rewards for the meritorious of the "Pacification of Difficulties," enfeoffed the various princes, and added military guards and the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, with the wars newly ended, the court debated rewards for the Jingnan meritorious, enfeoffed the princely domains, and expanded the military guards and myriad offices.

sentences.zh: 已，又發卒八十萬問罪安南、中官造巨艦通海外諸國、大起北都宮闕。

translations.literal: Then again he deployed eight hundred thousand troops to chastise Annam, had eunuchs build great ships to reach the various lands beyond the sea, and undertook on a grand scale the palace halls of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he again sent eight hundred thousand troops to punish Annam, had eunuchs build great ships to reach overseas states, and raised the palace halls of the Northern Capital on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 供億轉輸以鉅萬萬計，皆取給戶曹。

translations.literal: Provisions and transport ran to tens upon tens of millions—all drawn from the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies and transport costs ran into the tens of millions, all to be met by the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 原吉悉心計應之，國用不絀。

translations.literal: Yuanji with full heart calculated to meet them, and state expenditures did not run short.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji calculated every need with care, and the treasury never fell short.

sentences.zh: 六年命督軍民輸材北都，詔以錦衣官校從，治怠事者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to supervise military and civilian delivery of building materials to the Northern Capital; an edict had brocade-clad guard officers accompany [him] to punish the negligent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to oversee the delivery of building materials to the Northern Capital by soldiers and civilians; an edict sent brocade-clad guard officers with him to punish slackness.

sentences.zh: 原吉慮犯者眾，告戒而後行，人皆感悅。

translations.literal: Yuanji feared that offenders would be many; he gave warnings before acting, and all were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that many would offend, Yuanji issued warnings before setting out, and all were grateful and reassured.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝北巡，命兼攝行在禮部、兵部、都察院事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor toured the north and ordered [Yuanji] concurrently to oversee the affairs of the traveling palace Ministry of Rites, Ministry of War, and Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the emperor toured the north, Yuanji was ordered concurrently to handle the affairs of the traveling palace Ministries of Rites and War and of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有二指揮冒月廩，帝欲斬之。

translations.literal: Two commanders fraudulently drew monthly rations; the emperor wished to behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Two commanders had fraudulently drawn monthly rations, and the emperor wished to execute them.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「非律也，假實為盜，將何以加？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "It is not what the law provides—if borrowing were treated as robbery, what further penalty would apply?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "That is not what the law allows. If borrowing were treated as theft, what punishment would remain for actual theft?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon [the emperor] desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，輔太孫留守北京，總行在九卿事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor marched north; [Yuanji] assisted the Grand Heir Apparent in remaining to guard Beijing and oversaw the affairs of the Nine Ministers at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor marched north; Yuanji assisted the Grand Heir Apparent in guarding Beijing and directed the affairs of the Nine Ministers at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 時諸司草創，每旦，原吉入佐太孫參決庶務。

translations.literal: At that time the various offices were newly established; each morning Yuanji entered to assist the Grand Heir Apparent in deciding routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The offices were then still being established; each morning Yuanji entered to help the Grand Heir Apparent decide routine business.

sentences.zh: 朝退，諸曹郎御史環請事。

translations.literal: After court withdrew, department directors, secretaries, and censors surrounded him presenting business.
translations.idiomatic: After court, department directors, secretaries, and censors gathered round him with matters for decision.

sentences.zh: 原吉口答手書，不動聲色。

translations.literal: Yuanji answered by mouth and wrote by hand, without change of voice or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji answered aloud even as he wrote, never altering voice or expression.

sentences.zh: 北達行在，南啟監國，京師肅然。

translations.literal: Northward reports reached the traveling palace; southward he opened memorials to the regent—the capital was orderly and grave.
translations.idiomatic: Reports went north to the traveling palace; memorials went south to the regent—and the capital ran in sober order.

sentences.zh: 帝還，賜鈔幣、鞍馬、牢醴，慰勞有加。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned he bestowed paper money, saddle horses, and meat and wine, with especial consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he bestowed paper money, saddled horses, and meat and wine, rewarding Yuanji with special warmth.

sentences.zh: 尋從還南京，命侍太孫周行鄉落，觀民間疾苦。

translations.literal: Soon he accompanied [the emperor] back to Nanjing and was ordered to attend the Grand Heir Apparent touring villages to observe the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he accompanied the court back to Nanjing and was ordered to attend the Grand Heir Apparent on a tour of villages to witness the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 原吉取齏黍以進，曰：「願殿下食此，知民艱。

translations.literal: Yuanji took coarse millet and presented it, saying: "I hope Your Highness will eat this and know the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brought coarse millet and offered it, saying, "May Your Highness eat this and know the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 」九載滿，與蹇義皆宴便殿，帝指二人謂群臣曰：「高皇帝養賢以貽朕。

translations.literal: " When nine years in office were complete, he and Jian Yi were both feasted in the Informal Hall; the emperor pointed to the two and told the assembled ministers: "The High Emperor nurtured worthies to bequeath to me.
translations.idiomatic: When nine years of service were complete, he and Jian Yi were both feasted in the Informal Hall. The emperor pointed to the two and told the assembled ministers, "The High Emperor raised worthy men and left them to me."

sentences.zh: 欲觀古名臣，此其人矣。

translations.literal: If one wishes to see famous ministers of old, these are the men.
translations.idiomatic: If you would see the great ministers of antiquity, here they are."

sentences.zh: 」自是屢侍太孫，往來兩京，在道隨事納忠，多所裨益。

translations.literal: " From then on he often attended the Grand Heir Apparent, traveling between the two capitals; on the road he offered loyal counsel on whatever arose, to much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he often attended the Grand Heir Apparent, traveling between the two capitals and offering loyal counsel on whatever arose, to great benefit.

sentences.zh: 十八年，北京宮室成，使原吉南召太子、太孫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the palace halls of Beijing were completed; Yuanji was sent south to summon the Crown Prince and Grand Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Beijing palace was finished, Yuanji was sent south to summon the Crown Prince and Grand Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 既還，原吉言：「連歲營建，今告成。

translations.literal: After returning, Yuanji said: "Construction year after year—now it is declared complete.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yuanji said, "Construction has continued year after year; now it is declared complete.

sentences.zh: 宜撫流亡，蠲逋負以寬民力。

translations.literal: It is fitting to succor the displaced, remit overdue levies, and ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: It is time to succor the displaced, remit overdue taxes, and ease the people's burden."

sentences.zh: 」明年，三殿災，原吉復申前請，亟命所司行之。

translations.literal: " The next year the Three Main Halls burned; Yuanji again pressed his earlier request, and [the emperor] urgently ordered the relevant offices to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Three Main Halls burned. Yuanji renewed his earlier request, and the emperor urgently ordered the responsible offices to act on it.

sentences.zh: 初以殿災詔求直言，群臣多言都北京非便。

translations.literal: Initially, on account of the hall fire an edict solicited blunt counsel; many ministers said that making Beijing the capital was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: After the hall fire an edict first called for blunt counsel, and many ministers argued that keeping the capital at Beijing was unwise.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，殺主事蕭儀，曰：「方遷都時，與大臣密議，久而後定，非輕舉也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and executed Director Xiao Yi, saying: "When the capital was moved, we privately deliberated with great ministers; only after long discussion was it settled—not a light decision.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and executed Director Xiao Yi, saying, "When the capital was moved, I deliberated at length in secret with the senior ministers. It was no hasty decision."

sentences.zh: 」言者因劾大臣。

translations.literal: " The memorialists thereupon impeached the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The memorialists then impeached the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝命跪午門外質辨。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and answer the charges face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to kneel outside the Meridian Gate and answer the charges in person.

sentences.zh: 大臣爭詈言者，原吉獨奏曰：「彼應詔無罪。

translations.literal: The ministers quarreled and reviled the memorialists; Yuanji alone memorialized: "They responded to the edict—they are without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers quarreled and reviled the memorialists, but Yuanji alone submitted, "They answered the edict and are not guilty.

sentences.zh: 臣等備員大臣，不能協贊大計，罪在臣等。

translations.literal: We ministers hold places as nominal officers and failed to harmonize and support the grand design—the fault lies with us.
translations.idiomatic: We senior ministers failed to unite in support of the great plan—the fault is ours."

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，兩宥之。

translations.literal: " The emperor's anger eased, and he pardoned both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased, and he pardoned both sides.

sentences.zh: 或尤原吉背初議。

translations.literal: Some blamed Yuanji for betraying the original agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Some reproached Yuanji for going back on the earlier understanding.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾輩歷事久，言雖失，幸上憐之。

translations.literal: He said: "We have served long; though our words erred, fortunately the sovereign pities us.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "We have served long. Though our words were wrong, the emperor may yet show us mercy.

sentences.zh: 若言官得罪，所損不細矣。

translations.literal: If the remonstrating officers were punished, the loss would not be small.
translations.idiomatic: But if the remonstrating officers were punished, the harm would be far greater."

sentences.zh: 」眾始嘆服。

translations.literal: Only then did all sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the others sigh and acknowledge he was right.

sentences.zh: 原吉雖居戶部，國家大事輒令詳議。

translations.literal: Though Yuanji held office in the Revenue Ministry, on great affairs of state he was always ordered to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuanji served in the Ministry of Revenue, on great affairs of state he was always summoned to deliberate in detail.

sentences.zh: 帝每禦便殿闕門，召語移時，左右莫得聞。

translations.literal: The emperor often attended the informal hall at Que Gate and summoned him to converse for long stretches; those at hand could not hear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often received him at the Informal Hall by Que Gate and talked with him at length; those nearby could not hear what was said.

sentences.zh: 退則恂恂若無預者。

translations.literal: On retiring he was deferential, as if he had had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing he was modest and deferential, as though he had played no part in the matter.

sentences.zh: 交阯平，帝問：「遷官與賞孰便？

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the emperor asked: "Which is more expedient—transferring officials or giving rewards?
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi was pacified, the emperor asked, "Which is better—to transfer officials or to grant rewards?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「賞費於一時，有限；

translations.literal: Rewards cost at one time and are limited;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Rewards are a one-time expense and finite;

sentences.zh: 遷官為後日費，無窮也。

translations.literal: transferring officials becomes expense for later days, without end.
translations.idiomatic: transferring officials creates expense for years to come, without end."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] followed [this advice].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 西域法王來朝，帝欲郊勞，原吉不可。

translations.literal: The Dharma King of the Western Regions came to court; the emperor wished to greet him with suburban ceremony—Yuanji forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dharma King of the Western Regions came to court, the emperor wished to greet him with full suburban ceremony, but Yuanji objected.

sentences.zh: 及法王入，原吉見，不拜。

translations.literal: When the Dharma King entered, Yuanji saw him and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dharma King entered, Yuanji met him but did not bow.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿欲效韓愈耶？

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Do you wish to emulate Han Yu?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Do you mean to imitate Han Yu?"

sentences.zh: 」山東唐賽兒反，事平，俘脅從者三千余人至。

translations.literal: In Shandong Tang Sai'er rebelled; when the affair was settled, more than three thousand compelled followers taken captive were brought [to court].
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong Tang Sai'er rose in rebellion; when the affair was settled, more than three thousand coerced followers taken captive were brought to court.

sentences.zh: 原吉請於帝，悉原之。

translations.literal: Yuanji requested of the emperor that all be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji asked the emperor to pardon them all.

sentences.zh: 谷王叛，帝疑長沙有通謀者。

translations.literal: Prince of Gu Zhu Tan rebelled; the emperor suspected that in Changsha there were conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gu, Zhu Tan, rebelled, the emperor suspected conspirators in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 原吉以百口保之，乃得寢。

translations.literal: Yuanji guaranteed them with his hundred mouths [lives of his clan], and the matter was allowed to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji pledged the lives of his entire clan in their defense, and the investigation was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十九年冬，帝將大舉征沙漠。

translations.literal: In the winter of the nineteenth year the emperor was about to mount a great expedition against the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the nineteenth year the emperor planned a major campaign into the desert.

sentences.zh: 命原吉與禮部尚書呂震、兵部尚書方賓、工部尚書吳中等議，皆言兵不當出。

translations.literal: He ordered Yuanji together with Minister of Rites Lu Zhen, Minister of War Fang Bin, and Minister of Works Wu Zhong and others to deliberate—they all said the army ought not march out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yuanji, together with Ministers of Rites Lu Zhen, War Fang Bin, and Works Wu Zhong and others, to deliberate; all said the army should not march.

sentences.zh: 未奏，會帝召賓，賓力言軍興費乏，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Before they could memorialize, the emperor happened to summon Bin; Bin strongly stated that raising armies was costly and supplies scarce—the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could submit their report, the emperor summoned Fang Bin, who forcefully argued that war would strain supplies; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 召原吉問邊儲多寡，對曰：「比年師出無功，軍馬儲蓄十喪八九，災眚叠作，內外俱疲。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji and asked the amount of frontier stores; he replied: "In recent years campaigns have gone forth without success; of military stores nine or ten parts in ten are lost. Disasters have struck in succession; within and without all are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Yuanji and asked how much lay in frontier stores. Yuanji answered, "In recent years our armies have marched without success, and nine tenths of military stores are gone. Disasters have followed one upon another; court and country alike are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 況聖躬少安，尚須調護，乞遣將往征，勿勞車駕。

translations.literal: Moreover the sacred person has only lately been at ease and still needs tending—I beg that generals be sent to campaign and the imperial carriage not be troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty has only lately recovered and still needs care. I beg that generals be sent to campaign and that the imperial carriage not be put to the hardship."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，立命原吉出理開平糧儲。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately ordered Yuanji out to manage grain stores at Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and immediately ordered Yuanji out to manage grain stores at Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 而吳中入對如賓言，帝益怒。

translations.literal: Wu Zhong entered to answer as Bin had spoken—the emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zhong entered audience and spoke as Fang Bin had, the emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 召原吉系之內官監，並系大理丞鄒師顏，以嘗署戶部也。

translations.literal: He summoned Yuanji and imprisoned him in the Inner Palace Directorate, and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, because he had once held temporary charge of the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yuanji seized and imprisoned in the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs, and also imprisoned Assistant Minister of Justice Zou Shiyan, who had once acted for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 賓懼自殺。

translations.literal: Bin, in fear, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bin, in fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 遂並籍原吉家，自賜鈔外，惟布衣瓦器。

translations.literal: Thereupon they also inventoried Yuanji's household; apart from gifts of paper money, there were only plain clothes and earthenware.
translations.idiomatic: They then inventoried Yuanji's household; apart from imperial gifts of paper money, he owned only plain clothes and earthenware vessels.

sentences.zh: 明年北征，以糧盡引還。

translations.literal: The next year on the northern expedition, with provisions exhausted they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the northern campaign, supplies ran out and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已，復連歲出塞，皆不見敵。

translations.literal: Then again for successive years they went beyond the frontier, yet never sighted the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After that the emperor campaigned beyond the frontier year after year, yet never encountered the enemy.

sentences.zh: 還至榆木川，帝不豫，顧左右曰：「夏原吉愛我。

translations.literal: Returning to Yumu Stream, the emperor took ill and turned to those beside him, saying: "Xia Yuanji loves me.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Yumu Stream the emperor fell ill and, turning to those beside him, said, "Xia Yuanji truly cares for me."

sentences.zh: 」崩聞至之三日，太子走系所，呼原吉，哭而告之。

translations.literal: Three days after news of the imperial death arrived, the Crown Prince ran to the prison, called Yuanji, and weeping told him.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after word of the emperor's death arrived, the Crown Prince ran to the prison, called for Yuanji, and weeping told him the news.

sentences.zh: 原吉伏地哭，不能起。

translations.literal: Yuanji prostrated himself and wept, unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji prostrated himself and wept until he could not rise.

sentences.zh: 太子令出獄，與議喪禮，復問赦詔所宜。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ordered him released from prison to join in deliberating the funeral rites, and again asked what ought to be in the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ordered him released to help plan the funeral rites and again asked what the amnesty edict should contain.

sentences.zh: 對以振饑、省賦役、罷西洋取寶船及雲南、交阯采辦諸道金銀課。

translations.literal: He answered with relief for famine, reducing taxes and corvée, halting the Western Ocean treasure ships and the various routes for procuring gold and silver in Yunnan and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: famine relief, reduced taxes and corvée, an end to the Western Ocean treasure fleets, and the abolition of gold and silver procurement missions in Yunnan and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All were adopted.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，復其官。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, [Yuanji's] office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, Yuanji's office was restored.

sentences.zh: 方原吉在獄，有母喪，至是乞歸終制。

translations.literal: While Yuanji was in prison his mother died; at this point he requested return home to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanji was in prison his mother had died; he now asked leave to return home and observe full mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿老臣，當與朕共濟艱難。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old minister—you ought to share hardship with me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are a veteran minister and should share these hard times with me.

sentences.zh: 卿有喪，朕獨無喪乎？

translations.literal: You have mourning—do I alone have none?
translations.idiomatic: You have lost your mother—do you think I have lost nothing?"

sentences.zh: 」厚賜之，令家人護喪，馳傳歸葬，有司治喪事。

translations.literal: He richly rewarded him, ordered family members to escort the coffin, sent him post-horses to hurry home for burial, and had the officials manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yuanji rich gifts, ordered his family to escort the coffin, sent post-horses to hurry him home for burial, and had the officials manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 原吉不敢復言。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji did not dare raise the matter again.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 呂震以太子少師班原吉上，帝命鴻臚引震列其下。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen, as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, ranked above Yuanji; the emperor ordered the Director of Ceremonial to lead Zhen to stand below him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen, though senior as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, had ranked above Yuanji; the emperor ordered the Director of Ceremonial to conduct Lu Zhen to take his place below him.

sentences.zh: 進少保，兼太子少傅、尚書如故，食三祿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Guardian, concurrently Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Minister as before, with emoluments from three offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian, retaining his post as minister while also serving as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with emoluments from three offices.

sentences.zh: 原吉固辭，乃聽辭太子少傅祿。

translations.literal: Yuanji firmly declined; thereupon he was allowed to decline the Junior Preceptor's emolument.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji firmly declined; the emperor then allowed him to forgo the Junior Preceptor's stipend.

sentences.zh: 賜「繩愆糾繆」銀章，建第於兩京。

translations.literal: He was bestowed a silver seal inscribed "Correct faults and rectify errors," and residences were built for him in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He received a silver seal inscribed "Correct faults and rectify errors," and mansions were built for him in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 已而仁宗崩，太子至自南京。

translations.literal: Before long Renzong died; the heir arrived from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Renzong died, and the heir arrived from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 原吉奉遺詔迎於盧溝橋。

translations.literal: Yuanji, following the testamentary edict, welcomed [him] at the Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji, acting on the late emperor's testament, welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，以舊輔益親重。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, as an old supporter he was all the more intimate and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he treated Yuanji with still greater intimacy as a veteran counselor.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢王高煦反，亦以「靖難」為辭，移檄罪狀諸大臣，以原吉為首。

translations.literal: The next year Prince of Han Zhu Gaoxu rebelled, likewise taking "Pacification of Difficulties" as his plea; he circulated a proclamation listing the crimes of the great ministers, with Yuanji at the head.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled, likewise invoking the Jingnan precedent and issuing a manifesto condemning the senior ministers, with Yuanji named first.

sentences.zh: 帝夜召諸臣議。

translations.literal: At night the emperor summoned the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor summoned his ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 楊榮首勸帝親征。

translations.literal: Yang Rong was first to urge the emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong was the first to urge the emperor to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 帝難之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「獨不見李景隆已事耶？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Have you alone not seen what became of Li Jinglong?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "Have we not already seen what became of Li Jinglong?

sentences.zh: 臣昨見所遣將，命下即色變，臨事可知矣。

translations.literal: Yesterday I saw the generals you dispatched—when the order came down their faces changed; how they will fare in action is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I saw the generals you sent out—they turned pale the moment orders were issued. One can already tell how they will perform in battle.

sentences.zh: 且兵貴神速，卷甲趨之，所謂先人有奪人之心也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in warfare speed is prized; roll up armor and hurry there—this is what is called seizing the enemy's heart before he has his.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, war prizes speed. March at once in full armor—that is how one seizes the initiative before the enemy does.

sentences.zh: 榮策善。

translations.literal: Rong's plan is good.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's plan is sound.

sentences.zh: 」帝意遂決。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 師還，賚予加等，賜閽者三人。

translations.literal: When the army returned, rewards were increased by one grade, and three gatekeepers were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his rewards were raised one grade and three gatekeepers were granted him.

sentences.zh: 原吉以無功辭。

translations.literal: Yuanji declined on grounds of no merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji declined on the ground that he had earned no merit.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 三年，從北巡。

translations.literal: In the third year he accompanied the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he accompanied the northern inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 帝取原吉橐糗嘗之，笑曰：「何惡也？

translations.literal: The emperor took the dry rations from Yuanji's bag and tasted them, laughing: "How vile!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took dry rations from Yuanji's bag and tasted them, laughing, "How wretched is this!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「軍中猶有餒者。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In the army there are still men who starve.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji answered, "There are still hungry men in the army."

sentences.zh: 」帝命賜以大官之饌，且犒將士。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered that he be given food from the imperial kitchen and that the troops also be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered imperial kitchen fare bestowed on him and rewards given to the troops as well.

sentences.zh: 從閱武兔兒山，帝怒諸將慢，褫其衣。

translations.literal: Accompanying the review of troops at Tuer Mountain, the emperor was angry that the generals were disrespectful and stripped off their clothes.
translations.idiomatic: On accompanying a military review at Tuer Mountain, the emperor grew angry that the generals were disrespectful and ordered their garments stripped off.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「將帥，國爪牙，奈何凍而斃之？

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Generals and commanders are the state's claws and teeth—how can we freeze them to death?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "Generals are the state's claws and fangs—how can we let them freeze to death?"

sentences.zh: 」反覆力諫。

translations.literal: " He remonstrated repeatedly with force.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為卿釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For your sake I release them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For your sake I shall release them."

sentences.zh: 」再與蹇義同賜銀印，文曰：「含弘貞靖。

translations.literal: " Again he and Jian Yi were together bestowed silver seals inscribed "Broad, forbearing, upright, and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jian Yi were again granted silver seals together, inscribed "Broad, forbearing, upright, and tranquil."

sentences.zh: 」帝雅善繪事，嘗親畫《壽星圖》以賜。

translations.literal: " The emperor was skilled at painting and once personally painted the 《Star of Longevity》 to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was skilled at painting and once personally painted the 《Star of Longevity》 as a gift.

sentences.zh: 其他圖畫、服食、器用、銀幣、玩好之賜，無虛日。

translations.literal: Other gifts of paintings, food and drink, utensils, silver coins, and curios were bestowed without an idle day.
translations.idiomatic: Other gifts—paintings, food, utensils, silver, and curios—were bestowed almost every day.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，兩朝實錄成，復賜金幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were completed, he was again bestowed gold coins and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Veritable Records of the two reigns were completed, he received gold coins and saddle horses again.

sentences.zh: 旦入謝，歸而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: At dawn he entered to give thanks; returning home he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He went in at dawn to give thanks; on returning home he died, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚忠靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongjing (Loyal and Serene).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Serene.

sentences.zh: 敕戶部復其家，世世無所與。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Revenue Ministry to restore his household—generation after generation without taxation or corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to restore his household to prosperity, exempting his descendants forever from tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 原吉有雅景，人莫能測其際。

translations.literal: Yuanji had an elegant bearing; no one could fathom his inner reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji bore himself with quiet elegance; no one could plumb his inner depths.

sentences.zh: 同列有善，即采納之。

translations.literal: When a colleague had merit, he immediately adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a colleague had a good idea, he adopted it at once.

sentences.zh: 或有小過，必為之掩覆。

translations.literal: If there was a small fault, he always covered it for them.
translations.idiomatic: If someone slipped in a small matter, he always covered it for them.

sentences.zh: 吏汙所服金織賜衣。

translations.literal: A clerk stained the gold-woven robe he had been granted.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk stained the gold-woven robe the emperor had granted him.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「勿怖，汙可浣也。

translations.literal: Yuanji said: "Do not fear—stains can be washed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji said, "Do not be afraid—stains can be washed out."

sentences.zh: 」又有汙精微文書者，吏叩頭請死。

translations.literal: " Again there was one who stained a delicate official document; the clerk kowtowed begging for death.
translations.idiomatic: When another clerk stained a delicate official document, the man kowtowed begging for death.

sentences.zh: 原吉不問，自入朝引咎，帝命易之。

translations.literal: Yuanji did not inquire; he himself entered court to accept blame, and the emperor ordered it replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji made no inquiry but went to court himself to accept blame; the emperor ordered the document replaced.

sentences.zh: 呂震嘗傾原吉。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen once tried to undermine Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen had once tried to undermine Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 震為子乞官，原吉以震在「靖難」時有守城功，為之請。

translations.literal: When Zhen begged an office for his son, Yuanji, because Zhen had merit in defending the city during "Pacification of Difficulties," pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü begged an office for his son, Yuanji pleaded on his behalf because Lü had defended the city during the Jingnan campaigns.

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳瑄初亦惡原吉，原吉顧時時稱瑄才。

translations.literal: The Earl of Pingjiang Chen Xuan at first also disliked Yuanji, yet Yuanji would from time to time praise Xuan's talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, had at first disliked Yuanji, yet Yuanji often praised Chen's ability.

sentences.zh: 或問原吉：「量可學乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yuanji: "Can forbearance be learned?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Yuanji, "Can forbearance be learned?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾幼時，有犯未嘗不怒。

translations.literal: He said: "In my youth, when offended I never failed to grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In my youth I was never offended without growing angry.

sentences.zh: 始忍於色，中忍於心，久則無可忍矣。

translations.literal: At first I bore it in my face, then in my heart; after long practice there was nothing left I could not bear.
translations.idiomatic: At first I bore it in my face, then in my heart; in time there was nothing I could not endure."

sentences.zh: 」嘗夜閱爰書，撫案而嘆，筆欲下輒止。

translations.literal: Once at night he reviewed criminal dossiers, stroked the desk and sighed; the brush was about to descend yet he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night, reviewing criminal dossiers, he stroked the desk and sighed; his brush was poised to descend, then he stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 妻問之。

translations.literal: His wife asked him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked why.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此歲終大辟奏也。

translations.literal: He said: "This is the year-end memorial on capital punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is the year-end report on capital sentences."

sentences.zh: 」與同列飲他所，夜歸值雪，過禁門，有欲不下者，原吉曰：「君子不以冥冥墮行。

translations.literal: " Drinking with colleagues at another's house, he returned at night in snow; passing the forbidden gate, some wished not to dismount; Yuanji said: "A gentleman does not let his conduct fall in the dark.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking with colleagues elsewhere, he returned at night through snow. At the forbidden gate some wished not to dismount; Yuanji said, "A gentleman does not let his conduct fail in the dark."

sentences.zh: 」其慎如此。

translations.literal: " His caution was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 原吉與義皆起家太祖時。

translations.literal: Yuanji and Yi both rose from service in Taizu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji and Jian both began their careers under Taizu.

sentences.zh: 義秉銓政，原吉筦度支，皆二十七年，名位先於三楊。

translations.literal: Yi held the power of appointments; Yuanji managed expenditures—each for twenty-seven years, their fame and rank ahead of the Three Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian held the power of appointments; Yuanji managed the treasury—each for twenty-seven years, their standing ahead of the Three Yang.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之世，外兼臺省，內參館閣，與三楊同心輔政。

translations.literal: In the Ren and Xuan reigns, without they also held outer posts in the ministries and inner participation in the Hanlin, together with the Three Yang they assisted in government with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ren and Xuan they also held posts in the outer ministries and inner councils, and with the Three Yang they governed in concert.

sentences.zh: 義善謀，榮善斷，而原吉與士奇尤持大體，有古大臣風烈。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled in planning, Rong skilled in decision; Yuanji and Shiqi especially upheld the larger pattern, with the wind and stature of great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Jian excelled at planning, Rong at decision; Yuanji and Shiqi especially upheld the larger pattern, with the bearing of great ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 子瑄，以蔭為尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: His son Xuan, by hereditary privilege, became vice commissioner of the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan, by hereditary privilege, became vice commissioner of the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 喜談兵。

translations.literal: He delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in discussing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰時，數上章言兵事，有沮者，不獲用。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he several times memorialized on military affairs; there were obstructors, and [his advice] was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he repeatedly memorialized on military affairs, but opponents blocked his proposals and they were not adopted.

sentences.zh: 終南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 李文郁，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Li Wenyu was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenyu was a native of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以戶部侍郎副原吉治水有勞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, as Vice Minister of Revenue he assisted Yuanji in water control and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongle, as Vice Minister of Revenue he assisted Yuanji in water control and earned merit.

sentences.zh: 後坐事謫遼東二十年。

translations.literal: Later, on account of an offense he was banished to Liaodong for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was banished to Liaodong for twenty years on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召還，為南京通政參議，致仕。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he was recalled and made Nanjing Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne he was recalled, appointed Nanjing Vice Commissioner of the Transmission Office, and later retired.

sentences.zh: 鄒師顏，宣都人。

translations.literal: Zou Shiyan was a man of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shiyan was a native of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，為江西參政，坐事免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was Jiangxi Administrative Commissioner and was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongle he served as Jiangxi Administrative Commissioner and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋以薦擢御史，有直聲。

translations.literal: Soon, on recommendation, he was promoted to censor and had a reputation for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on recommendation, he was promoted to censor and gained a reputation for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞，署戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Minister of Justice and held temporary charge of the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Minister of Justice and temporarily acted for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與原吉同下獄。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned together with Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned together with Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，釋為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he was released and made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne he was released and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 省墓歸，還至通州，卒，貧不能歸葬。

translations.literal: Returning from tending his parents' graves, he reached Tongzhou and died, too poor to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from tending his parents' graves he reached Tongzhou and died, too poor to transport his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震聞於朝，宣宗命驛舟送之。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Zhen reported it to court; Xuanzong ordered a courier boat to convey the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Zhen reported this to court; Emperor Xuanzong ordered a courier boat to convey his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 詔京官卒者，皆給驛，著為令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when capital officials died, all should be given courier service—established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that when capital officials died, courier transport should be provided for their funerals, and this was made a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《書》曰「敷求哲人，俾輔於爾後嗣」。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The 《Book》 says, "Seek out the wise broadly and set them to assist your successor.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The 《Book of Documents》 says, "Seek out the wise broadly and set them to assist your successor."

sentences.zh: 蹇義、夏原吉自筮仕之初，即以誠篤幹濟受知太祖，至成祖，益任以繁劇。

translations.literal: Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji from the beginning of their divined service were known to Taizu for sincere integrity and practical ability; reaching Chengzu, they were all the more entrusted with heavy duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the very start of their careers Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji won Taizu's trust through sincerity and practical ability; under Chengzu their burdens grew still heavier.

sentences.zh: 而二人實能通達政體，諳練章程，稱股肱之任。

translations.literal: Yet the two men truly could penetrate the structure of government and were thoroughly versed in regulations—worthy to be called arms and thighs of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Both men truly understood how government worked and were thoroughly versed in regulations—they were rightly called the state's right hand.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣繼體，委寄優隆，同德協心，匡翼令主。

translations.literal: Renzong and Xuanzong succeeded in turn; their trust and charge were generous, and with one virtue and one heart they aided and corrected their enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ren and Xuan their trust was generous; with one heart they aided and corrected enlightened rulers.

sentences.zh: 用使吏治修明，民風和樂，成績懋著，蔚為宗臣。

translations.literal: By this the governance of officials was made clear, the people's customs harmonious and joyful, achievements splendid and marked—they stood eminent among the dynasty's great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Through them official governance was clarified, the people's customs harmonized, and their achievements stood splendid—they ranked among the dynasty's greatest ministers.

sentences.zh: 樹人之效，遠矣哉。

translations.literal: The effect of nurturing men—how far-reaching!
translations.idiomatic: The fruit of nurturing worthy men—how far its reach!
